title: Claude Meetings: How to Automate Your Workday with Claude Cowork
summary: Claude meetings integration allows you to assign live tasks to AI agents during video calls. You can determine if this tool fits your team's workflow.
body_markdown:
## How to connect Claude Meetings to your existing workflows


Claude Meetings integrates with enterprise automation by exposing meeting data as actionable triggers within a centralized orchestration canvas. This shift allows teams to move from passive recording to active workflow injection where a verbal agreement in a call initiates a sequence across distinct software platforms.


### Option 1: using the HTTP integration for API webhooks


The HTTP integration is the primary bridge for developers who need to capture raw meeting events from Claude Meetings as they occur. By configuring a Webhook trigger, you can ingest structured JSON payloads (containing speaker diarization and timestamped intent) directly into a workflow.


Real-time routing is fastest with this method. An "urgent" tag identified during a live session hits a notification queue without waiting for a batch sync.


The following workflow demonstrates how an AI-driven trigger translates a conversation into a cross-platform sequence:


The canvas shows a seven-step workflow: 1. New Lead (HubSpot trigger), 2. Qualify Lead (AI Agent step with purple border), 3. Qualified? (Condition), 4. Add to Salesforce, 5. Notify Slack, 6. Nurture Lead (Loop), and 7. Send Email (Gmail).


Steps are connected by vertical lines showing the flow logic.\]


Activepieces places an Agent step alongside deterministic automation steps inside one flow definition, ensuring judgment and rules run on the same engine.


Companies like MoneyGram and FundingSocieties run this in production to maintain a single execution trace for their meeting-driven workflows, rather than bridging two products with a webhook.


### Connecting Claude Sonnet via OpenAI-compatible AI steps


Standardized AI steps let you swap the underlying model logic while maintaining the same integration hooks for your meeting data.


By utilizing the OpenAI-compatible provider setting, you can point a workflow step toward the Claude Sonnet 5.5 API for complex reasoning or Claude Haiku 5.5 for high-speed classification tasks.


The intelligence layer remains modular with this configuration. You can use Claude Fable 5.2 for long-horizon agentic work.


### Using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with Claude


Claude Meetings can securely query and write to local or private data sources that lack public webhooks using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.


This protocol is a standardized interface, allowing the AI to fetch context from a local database or a proprietary file system to enrich a meeting summary before it is sent to a downstream tool.


By deploying an MCP server, you provide the model with a secure "reading room" where it can verify meeting claims against historical records without exposing that sensitive internal data to the public internet.
